canonicalization.accepted_citation_order: proposal premise_ids in their model-emitted order followed by accepted support_row_ids in their supplied additional_rows order, with first-occurrence deduplication over that concatenation; ASCII sorting is forbidden

atom_namespaces.anchor_rule: both anchor positions are animal: atoms; anchor: is not a legal namespace

public_projection.event_to_row_transform: copy kind and fields; set origin=WITNESSED,status=WITNESSED,support_basis=WITNESS,citations=[],depth=0; compute semantic_hash and record_hash; assign the sole actual-count mapping row_id

event_to_row_mapping.sole_algorithm: Let actual_event_count be the number of public events emitted by the sole public_projection_contract projector for this life; require 1<=actual_event_count<=49. For every and only integer i in 0..actual_event_count-1, map Ei='E'+zero_pad_6(i) bijectively to Mi='M'+zero_pad_6(i). No fixture-local, heldout-local, truncated, gapped, reused, or alternate mapping exists.
event_to_row_mapping.registered_lexical_domain: E000000..E000048 and M000000..M000048. E000049, M000049, and every higher witnessed alias are always rejected.
event_to_row_mapping.actual_count_closure: An alias with index i>=actual_event_count is rejected for that life even when i<=48. Seed-1 DEV with 49 events therefore requires E000048->M000048; seed-5 heldout with 46 events instantiates only indices 0..45 and rejects 46..48.
required_invariants: one-to-one and onto the produced event and witnessed-row sets

public_projection.timing: for event index i, seal Ei and Mi before WAKE slot i
public_projection.model_visibility: only the witnessed M row projection is supplied after projection; raw keys, event IDs, and lineage are not rendered

external_lineage_manifest.visibility: host-only and offline-scorer-only; never rendered to DREAM, SELF_CHECK, THINK, compiler views, selectors, or candidate completions
external_lineage_manifest.witnessed: lineage(Mi)=[Ei] under the sole actual-count event_to_row_mapping
external_lineage_manifest.dreamed: Traverse citations in the accepted row's stored premise-then-support order; lineage(row) is the ASCII-byte-sorted unique event-ID union of lineage(citation). Citation order is never re-sorted even though the derived event-ID set is canonically sorted.
external_lineage_manifest.manifest_hash: lowerhex(SHA256(UTF8(JCS(entries sorted by external life namespace, origin branch, row_id))))

slot_identity.branch_identity: PREFIX for slots 0-83; OWN or DIST for slots 84-99; external branch makes the repeated local alias unambiguous

dream_output_union: one CREATE object validating dream_operation.schema.json and its derived immutable proposal validating proposal.schema.json
proposal_and_acceptance.dream_create_to_proposal: for a schema-valid dream_operation CREATE, the harness assigns proposal_id and slot, copies kind/fields/citations, computes semantic_hash, copies prediction to audit_prediction and confidence to audit_confidence, computes proposal_hash, and then validates proposal.schema.json
proposal_and_acceptance.citation_eligibility: 2-8 distinct M row IDs, in model-emitted order, all owned and eligible in the same life/branch or ancestor before the proposal slot; E IDs, forward IDs, self IDs, cross-life IDs, and unregistered-branch IDs are rejected
proposal_and_acceptance.newness_key: external life namespace plus branch-visible semantic_hash set: PREFIX owns one set through slot 83; OWN and DIST each initialize by copying the complete PREFIX set, then independently add branch-local keys through slots 84-99
proposal_and_acceptance.fixed_self_check_opportunity_pairs: Before the first HELDOUT_TEXT provider dispatch, seal exactly one SELF_CHECK partner for each sealed DREAM opportunity using the identical stage, external life, origin branch, and proposal slot and profile=SELF_CHECK. The two heldout lives each contribute 84 PREFIX plus 16 OWN plus 16 DIST pairs = 116; total DREAM/SELF_CHECK pairs=232. Observing DREAM output can never add, delete, rename, re-pair, or double-effect a SELF_CHECK opportunity.
proposal_and_acceptance.first_schema_valid_proposal: if semantic_hash is absent from the current branch-visible key set, append one immutable proposal audit record, reserve it in that set, and dispatch the already registered paired SELF_CHECK exactly once
proposal_and_acceptance.duplicate_proposal: append DUPLICATE_PROPOSAL audit receipt, dispatch no SELF_CHECK, create no row, and record the prospectively paired SELF_CHECK as NON_DISPATCH_DUPLICATE/NON_DISPATCH_DUPLICATE/DUPLICATE_PROPOSAL with cause_opportunity_id equal to its exact DREAM partner and attempts/input_tokens/output_tokens all zero and provider_request_id null
proposal_and_acceptance.dream_pass: create no proposal and no row; record the prospectively paired SELF_CHECK as NON_DISPATCH_SELF_CHECK_NO_PROPOSAL/NON_DISPATCH_NOT_APPLICABLE/DREAM_PASS_NO_PROPOSAL with cause_opportunity_id equal to its exact DREAM partner, zero attempts/tokens, and null provider_request_id
proposal_and_acceptance.malformed_or_illegal_proposal: append the DREAM audit receipt, create no proposal and no row, and record the prospectively paired SELF_CHECK as NON_DISPATCH_SELF_CHECK_INVALID_PROPOSAL/NON_DISPATCH_NOT_APPLICABLE/DREAM_INVALID_NO_PROPOSAL with cause_opportunity_id equal to its exact DREAM partner, zero attempts/tokens, and null provider_request_id
proposal_and_acceptance.upstream_non_dispatch: Precondition, authority, and registered stage-wide conditions outrank DREAM-result-specific routes and retain their canonical condition, reason, and cause semantics. When a dispatched DREAM ends in infrastructure invalidity, the pair is NON_DISPATCH_POST_INFRASTRUCTURE_INVALIDITY/NON_DISPATCH_POST_INVALID/PRIOR_INFRASTRUCTURE_INVALIDITY with the exact DREAM partner as cause. No non-dispatch route constructs or sends a SELF_CHECK request.
proposal_and_acceptance.accounting_is_not_verification: Fixed pairing and its deterministic ledger reducer inspect only dispatch eligibility and structural validity. They never inspect truth, entailment, offline score, private state, or outcome and do not add a verifier, retry, or model call.
proposal_and_acceptance.self_check_input: the proposal cognitive projection; its cited accepted rows in identical citation order; and 0-8 additional eligible non-premise accepted rows in semantic_hash then row_id ASCII order

self_check_output.premise_ids: must byte-equal the proposal citations in identical order
self_check_output.support_row_ids: ordered unique array of 0-8 M IDs; when nonempty it MUST be a subsequence of the supplied additional_rows sequence and preserve that relative order
self_check_output.prediction: audit-only printable ASCII string of 1-192 characters
self_check_output.reason: audit-only printable ASCII string of 1-256 characters

structural_reducer.harness_check: no semantic entailment check and no additional support requirement

structural_reducer.support_row_ids: one or more IDs forming an order-preserving subsequence of supplied additional_rows; at least one named row has nonempty external lineage disjoint from the union of every proposal-citation lineage; the first-occurrence-deduplicated premise_ids then support_row_ids concatenation contains at most eight IDs
structural_reducer.harness_check: IDs, supplied-set membership, supplied relative order, eligibility, deduplicated concatenation cardinality at most eight, nonempty lineage, and set disjointness only; never truth or semantic entailment

proposal_and_acceptance.all_other_combinations: INVALID_SELF_CHECK audit receipt; no accepted row; no retry
proposal_and_acceptance.accepted_citation_union: Concatenate proposal citations in emitted premise order with accepted SELF_CHECK support_row_ids in their supplied additional_rows order, then preserve the first occurrence of each ID and discard only later occurrences; require 2-8 resulting IDs or classify INVALID_SELF_CHECK. This exact sequence is the accepted row citations array. Sorting by row ID, semantic hash, lineage, or any other key is forbidden.
proposal_and_acceptance.accepted_row_transform: copy reserved row_id, proposal kind, and proposal fields; set citations to accepted_citation_union; set origin=DREAMED,status=SUPPORTED,support_basis=the accepted claim; set depth=1+max(depth of every row in accepted_citation_union); copy proposal semantic_hash; compute record_hash
proposal_and_acceptance.cardinality: each proposal creates either zero rows or exactly one immutable accepted row; an accepted row never changes status, basis, citations, depth, semantic_hash, or record_hash
proposal_and_acceptance.proposal_acceptance_binding: append one host-only immutable entry {external_life_namespace,origin_branch,proposal_id,proposal_hash,self_check_receipt_hash,outcome,accepted_row_id,accepted_record_hash}; outcome is ACCEPTED with both accepted fields populated exactly once or REJECTED/INVALID/DUPLICATE with both accepted fields null
proposal_and_acceptance.audit_separation: SELF_CHECK prose, prediction, confidence, and receipts are audit-only and cannot enter cognition, selectors, compiler views, candidates, or training; support_row_ids affect cognition only through the canonical accepted-row citations union and its derived depth and external lineage, never as separately rendered SELF_CHECK state
proposal_and_acceptance.semantic_owner: among accepted rows with the same semantic_hash in one external life and current branch ancestry, the earliest owned row is canonical; PREFIX ownership suppresses the same semantic in both descendants, while a semantic first proposed after the fork may be independently owned once in OWN and once in DIST
proposal_and_acceptance.conflicting_missing_values: different semantic hashes remain separate canonical rows and are resolved as CONFLICT when the same legal one-null query matches multiple values

reader.query: one object {kind,fields} with exact row arity, exactly one JSON null, and valid typed atoms at every other index
reader.eligible_rows: canonical accepted rows with status WITNESSED or SUPPORTED in the mounted sealed semantic-row manifest
reader.match: kind byte equality, arity equality, and atom byte equality at every non-null index
resolution: collect matches and group by byte-exact missing-field value
one distinct value -> choose the earliest-owned canonical row for that value and return ROW
two or more distinct values -> CONFLICT
reader.read_handle: H plus the zero-padded six-digit thinker operation ordinal; one handle is allocated for each executed QUERY, regardless of result
reader.thinker_result: one backend-neutral exact JCS object validating read_result.schema.json; text and LoRA must produce byte-identical JCS for the same semantic outcome and handle
reader.scratch_reference: QUERY nodes cite read_handle only; row IDs are illegal thinker citations
reader.offline_handle_binding: after the complete trace seals, seal a host-only map from trace hash and read_handle to query hash, backend manifest hash, result type, and selected row semantic_hash/row_id or null

backend_neutral_atomic_read_projection.atomicity: Resolve exactly one query against exactly one mounted semantic manifest and, when required, exactly one mounted adapter plus exact roster; construct exactly one complete read_result; unmount; expose only that complete JCS result to the 32B thinker. No partial match, roster, score, backend, or provenance state is rendered.
backend_neutral_atomic_read_projection.projection: NOT_FOUND and CONFLICT expose only {type,read_handle}; ROW exposes only {type,read_handle,kind,fields,status,semantic_hash}. The read_handle is request-local and every semantic field is copied from the selected canonical semantic row.
backend_neutral_atomic_read_projection.backend_neutrality: For equal read_handle and equal semantic outcome, text, own-adapter, and donor-adapter resolution MUST emit byte-identical JCS bytes. Backend selection remains only in the sealed offline_handle_binding.
backend_neutral_atomic_read_projection.failure: Any extra field, partial result, multiple result, pre-unmount exposure, or backend-dependent byte is INVALID_INFRASTRUCTURE; no thinker dispatch consumes it.

candidate_winner_mapping.registry_timing: build prospectively from both sealed M1_OWN manifests and seal before final-goal reveal and before either fit
candidate_winner_mapping.required_rosters: exact set equality: exactly one roster for every unique realized compiler [semantic_hash,view_id,missing_index] cue instance across the two backend manifests and no extra roster; binding keys and roster_ids are each unique, and no roster object may be reused across keys
candidate_winner_mapping.roster_binding_validation: Before fitting or scoring, byte-compare roster semantic_hash, view_id, missing_index, cue_utf8_hex, cue_sha256, cue_token_ids, and cue_token_ids_sha256 with the exact compiler vector. Reject missing, duplicate, swapped, wrong-semantic, wrong-view, wrong-missing-index, wrong-cue, wrong-token, or reused-roster cases.
candidate_winner_mapping.value_universe: ASCII-byte-sorted unique values appearing at kind/missing_index across both backend manifests, followed by the NOT_FOUND sentinel
candidate_winner_mapping.candidate_bytes: VALUE uses ASCII(' ')||UTF8(JCS({value:value}))||ASCII('\n') followed by tokenizer EOS for scoring; NOT_FOUND uses ASCII(' ')||UTF8(JCS({not_found:true}))||ASCII('\n') followed by tokenizer EOS
candidate_winner_mapping.cue: the exact requested-view and missing-index cue from compiler_views.json for fidelity; online thinker reads use the QUESTION_RECOGNITION instance at the query's sole null index
pre_score_manifest_resolution: apply the text reader's exact kind, arity, and non-null atom match against the mounted semantic-only backend manifest
zero distinct missing-field values -> NOT_FOUND without adapter scoring
two or more distinct missing-field values -> CONFLICT without adapter scoring
exactly one distinct missing-field value -> score the sealed roster; only the adapter-selected completion may materialize the row
candidate_winner_mapping.scoring: teacher-forced full-token conditional log likelihood over candidate completion plus EOS; float32 log_softmax, float64 sum, divided by scored-token count
candidate_winner_mapping.winner: unique greatest mean score; every score within 1e-7 of the greatest belongs to the maximum set
candidate_winner_mapping.tie: two or more maximum candidates -> CONFLICT
candidate_winner_mapping.value_candidate_lookup: replace the query null with selected candidate.value, recompute semantic_hash, and look up byte-identical kind+fields in the mounted backend manifest only
lookup_resolution: selected NOT_FOUND or a selected value unequal to the unique pre-score manifest value -> NOT_FOUND
the selected unique manifest value has exactly one canonical semantic row -> ROW projection
any disagreement with the pre-score zero/one/multiple classification -> INVALID_INFRASTRUCTURE
candidate_winner_mapping.donor_semantics: L-TWIN performs the same lookup only in the donor adapter's bound backend manifest; absence in that backend is NOT_FOUND even if present in the recipient manifest
candidate_winner_mapping.host_enumerated_candidate_disclosure: The host first resolves zero, one, or multiple manifest values. Only the one-value case reaches the 7B scorer, which receives a shared host-enumerated two-backend answer roster containing every registered candidate answer completion for that exact cue instance. This is closed multiple-choice recognition, not open recall or weight-only retrieval, and the identical union roster carries no backend-membership or donor-identity labels.
candidate_winner_mapping.host_text_firewall: the 32B thinker receives only read_result.schema.json bytes; roster values, row IDs, citations, lineage, candidate scores, backend identity, and host provenance are never rendered
candidate_winner_mapping.backend_neutral_projection_identity: ROW uses the same status and semantic fields as text resolution; no adapter-only alias or provenance field exists. This byte-interface identity does not imply text/LoRA substrate equivalence.

transport_corpora.source: each life's already sealed M1_OWN canonical accepted rows projected immediately to semantic-only backend rows
transport_corpora.shared_semantic_manifest_rule: for a mounted backend, text resolution, candidate lookup, compiler input, fidelity expectations, and LoRA ROW materialization all reference the same sealed ordered {kind,fields,status,semantic_hash} projection; no backend-specific semantic copy may diverge
transport_corpora.immutability: row manifests, compiler vectors, fidelity cases, candidate registry, and state-token vocabularies seal before final-goal reveal and cannot change after any T or L result
transport_corpora.state_tokens: ASCII-byte-sorted unique label: field values in recipient M0 witnessed RECIPE rows; recipient vocabulary is reused byte-identically for its T and L arms
transport_corpora.compiler_input_exclusions: all fields excluded by compiler_views.json, including provenance and final-goal information

per_life_lora_isolation.fit_binding: one rank-64 adapter per scored life, trained only from that life's fixed M1_OWN compiler examples and a separately reloaded pristine Qwen2.5-7B base
per_life_lora_isolation.pooling: forbidden; each adapter independently must pass 44/48
per_life_lora_isolation.conditional_lifecycle: After valid reviewed Stage-T (HELDOUT_TO_LORA) authority and before either fit or fidelity request, seal exactly 48 THINK1_LORA opportunity IDs (two lives * L-OWN/L-TWIN * slots 0..11) as REGISTERED_NOT_DISPATCHABLE. The complete sealed registry is a precondition to both fits and all fidelity cases. Absent an infrastructure invalidity, complete and seal both fits and all 96 fidelity cases before evaluating the joint gate; both adapters must independently pass before every entry transitions together to DISPATCH_AUTHORIZED and before any L-OWN or L-TWIN thinker dispatch.
per_life_lora_isolation.fidelity_failure_accounting: If either separate 44/48 gate fails, every one of the 48 already registered L opportunities receives exactly one zero-attempt NON_DISPATCH_STAGE_FIDELITY_FAILURE/NON_DISPATCH_STAGE_FAILURE/FIDELITY_GATE_FAILED row. No entry dispatches, no partial authorization exists, and no replacement or retry is permitted.
atomic_mount_cycle: perform the semantic-manifest zero/one/multiple pre-score resolution
for a unique-value query verify pristine base and no adapter
score exactly one cue and its sealed roster
verify pristine base before the next clean 32B operation
per_life_lora_isolation.thinker_request_equivalence: for a fixed recipient, L-OWN and L-TWIN begin with byte-identical initial 32B request state and always use the same model snapshot, prompt, schemas, generation config, reducer, and seed rules; operation-locally, whenever their complete pre-read state and emitted query are byte-identical, only the host-side mounted adapter/backend binding may differ during that atomic read; differing read results and every causally downstream scratch, request, query, terminal, and trace byte are authorized treatment descendants
per_life_lora_isolation.maximum_atomic_recognition_cycles: F scored fidelity cycles plus Q scored online unique-value query cycles, where 0<=F<=96 and 0<=Q<=48, hence at most 144; all 96 fidelity cases are evaluated even when pre-score resolution avoids a mount; every actual cycle independently mounts, scores exactly one cue roster, records a receipt, unmounts, and verifies the pristine base
lifecycle_negatives: fit or fidelity before all 48 entries seal
not exactly one fidelity-failure row for each registered entry

lora_claim_boundary.maximum_supported_claim: For each of exactly two isolated per-life adapters, immediate host-pre-resolved candidate-constrained training-set-resubstitution recognition on the prospectively selected 48 registered cue instances passed at least 44/48, and the only evaluated decision paths were the registered own-adapter and donor-adapter paths.
mandatory_disclosures_in_every_lora_term: each 48-case set is training-derived resubstitution: exactly twelve selected M1_OWN rows per life crossed with the same four compiler view families used to train that life adapter
the selected rows and four view families received repeated exposure in that adapter's training examples; no fidelity cue is an unseen row or unseen view-family evaluation
the host pre-resolved zero, one, or multiple manifest values before any adapter score
the scorer received the shared host-enumerated two-backend answer-bearing roster for the exact cue instance
the fidelity set contained 48 prospectively selected registered cues per life
the per-life pass threshold was 44 correct of 48 and pooling was forbidden
only registered own-adapter and donor-adapter decision paths were evaluated
forbidden_claims: unseen-row, unseen-cue, held-out, or preservation evaluation
lora_claim_boundary.scope: The roster, cue selection, threshold, and own/donor paths support only this bounded recognition statement; neither a positive nor a negative result may be broadened beyond it.

mutate_without_effect: rendered final question bytes before authorized reveal
noninterference.exhaustive_cross_cue_roster_mutation: For each concrete realized cue instance, present the roster from every other concrete cue instance as an attempted substitution while public pre-reveal inputs remain fixed. Binding validation MUST reject every attempt before it replaces the sealed registry or reaches a consumer; the sealed candidate registry binding and every other pre-reveal byte remain unchanged. The adversarial input and rejection receipt are test/audit artifacts, not cognitive or transport state.
must_remain_byte_identical: later cognitive rows before authorized reveal
text read-result bytes for an unchanged text reader
LoRA thinker read-result bytes for an unchanged mounted adapter/backend binding
later 32B provider messages outside causally downstream treatment descendants
authorized_differences: registered OWN versus public DIST focus
mounted own versus donor adapter/backend binding
read results and later scratch, requests, queries, terminals, and trace bytes causally downstream of an authorized reader or mount difference
noninterference.failure: INVALID_PRECONDITION before affected dispatch; no repair or fallback

P1CB02 proves registered taint noninterference, not absence of this disclosed agenda cue or autonomous relevance discovery.
p1cb02_noninterference.authorized_exclusion: Only registered causal descendants after the authorized final-question reveal or an authorized reader/mount treatment may differ.

atomic_query_and_result_branches.query_expansion_rule: For every positive template, replace exactly each listed index with null in a separate object {kind,fields}; every expanded query MUST validate exactly that kind branch and no other branch at every applicable validation site.

positive_result_branches.result_generation: For each positive query template, construct {type:ROW,read_handle:H000003,kind,fields:complete_fields,status:WITNESSED,semantic_hash}; it MUST validate exactly the ROW branch for that kind.

claim_boundary.positive_terminal: The fidelity cases were training-derived resubstitution: exactly twelve selected M1_OWN training rows per life crossed with the same four repeatedly exposed trained compiler view families, for 48 cues per life. The host pre-resolved zero/one/multiple values; each scorer used the shared answer-bearing roster, each life had a separate 44/48 threshold, and only registered own/donor decision paths were evaluated. This supports immediate host-pre-resolved candidate-constrained training-set-resubstitution recognition only.
